diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\exists b\in\mathbb{R}\qquad u\left(  r\xi\right)  -b\log r\leq Cr^{-1}
\quad\text{as }r\rightarrow\infty\text{ uniformly in }\xi\in S_{1}.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated condition is not meaningful for complex-valued u because it orders a complex quantity, and even if the missing modulus is supplied, requiring b to be real contradicts well-posedness for all complex H^{1/2} data. For example, constant boundary data g=i require the logarithmic coefficient i/log R in the displayed solution, which is not real.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by an absolute-value estimate and allow b to be complex; then verify the well-posedness and DtN statements with that corrected condition.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted complex-valued solution operator Slog, the associated logarithmic DtN operator, and the lemma comparing it with the strong-condition DtN operator are not established under the radiation condition as defined.
issues.title: The two-dimensional logarithmic radiation condition excludes complex boundary data
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the radiation-condition definition accommodates exactly the solutions subsequently constructed and preserves the stated scope and formulas.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\left\vert z_{m,\nu}\left(  s\right)  \right\vert
  \leq C_{2}\left(  n\right)  \left(  m+1\right)  +\left\vert s\right\vert

The continuity of the DtN operator in the wavenumber $s\in\mathbb{C}_{\geq0}$
follows from Lebesgue's dominated convergence theorem for the absolutely
convergent series~(\ref{eqn:DtN_gh}) with spectral coefficients $z_{m,\nu}(s)$
dominated by (\ref{eqn:z_m_n_absolute_bound}).

issues.failure_explanation: Dominated convergence applied after fixing g and h proves continuity of each scalar pairing. It does not prove convergence in the operator norm from H^{1/2} to H^{-1/2}, which requires a uniform estimate over all modes and all unit vectors. The displayed domination grows like m and supplies no uniform small bound for z_{m,nu}(s)-z_{m,nu}(s_0).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken the claims explicitly to continuity of all duality pairings, or supply a uniform-in-m estimate for the differences of the spectral coefficients that proves operator-norm convergence.
issues.overall_effect: Operator-norm continuity and the operator-limit interpretation of the limit at zero remain unsupported; only weak-operator continuity follows from the supplied argument.
issues.title: Only scalar weak continuity of the DtN family is proved
issues.why_classification: The source supports a comparable weak continuity statement, but preserving the stated operator continuity requires an additional nontrivial uniform spectral argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
This proof considers the unit disc $S_{1}$ ($R=1$) and the general case $R>0$
follows from the scaling of the norms and the arising constants then also depend
on $R$.

issues.failure_explanation: For constant g at s=0, the spectral formulas give DtN(0)g=-(n-2)g/R. Thus the claimed lower bound becomes (n-2)/2 <= (n-2)/R, which is false when n>2 and R>2. The unit-sphere proof was transferred without the required factor 1/R.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the appropriate factor 1/R in the lower bound and consistently rescale the other radius-dependent constants.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative lower definiteness estimate in the main DtN theorem is false for general radii, although its positivity for n>=3 survives with the correct radius-dependent constant.
issues.title: The DtN coercivity bound omits the radius scaling
issues.why_classification: The explicit spectral formula forces a short local rescaling correction, with no loss of positivity, scope, or downstream qualitative guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: The source defines gamma_1 only on H^1(omega,Delta), so gamma_1 v is not defined for an arbitrary H^1 function used in DefH1Gamma. Moreover, membership asks only for an H^{-1/2} trace while the announced norm takes its L^2 norm, which need not exist. Consequently the quantified domain and its Hilbert topology are not mathematically defined.

failure_location.quote:
Any $v\in H^{1}\left(  \Omega,S_{R}\right)  $ with

$\partial_{r}v=\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)  v$ on $S_{R}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define a legitimate space on which a weak normal trace exists, with an H^{-1/2} graph norm, or impose a local H^1(Delta) hypothesis near S_R; then restate the boundary condition and proofs in that space.
issues.overall_effect: The Friedrichs theorem and the corollary relying on it lack a valid function-space domain and graph norm.
issues.title: The function space used in the Friedrichs theorem is ill-defined
issues.why_classification: Repair requires a genuine domain definition or an additional regularity hypothesis, not merely notation, but it can be localized near the artificial boundary without changing the intended estimate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Since this sequence is bounded in $H$, it admits a weakly convergent
subsequence with weak limit $u\in H$.

Because $u\in H$, there exists $s\in\mathbb{C}_{\geq0}$ with
$\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)    u  =\partial_{r}u$.

issues.failure_explanation: H is a union over z of different graph subspaces and is generally neither a vector space nor closed, so continuity of each DtN(z) does not make it a Hilbert space. The parameters associated with v_k may vary and need not converge, hence a weak limit need not satisfy a DtN condition for any fixed s. In addition, negating the stated estimate yields convergence of the normal traces in H^{-1/2}, not the stronger L^2 convergence assumed in the proof.

H=\left\{  v\in H^{1}\left(  \Omega,S_{R}\right)  \mid\partial_{r}
v-\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  z\right)  v=0\ \text{ on }S_{R}\text{ for some

\]
(The completeness of $H$ follows from the continuity of the
$\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)  $ operator by \Cref{thm:DtN}.)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the union-space compactness argument by a uniform argument, for example using the DtN real-part coercivity to control the boundary trace directly from its H^{-1/2} normal trace, followed by a standard Poincare estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The contradiction argument does not prove the uniform-in-s Friedrichs estimate, and therefore does not support the corollary derived from it.
issues.title: The compactness proof treats a union of DtN graph spaces as a Hilbert space
issues.why_classification: The theorem may be recoverable by a contained replacement argument, but the present proof's central compactness construction is invalid and cannot be fixed by a local edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Consider a bounded
Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ in $n\geq3$ dimensions such
that $S_{R}\subset\partial\Omega$ is relatively closed in $\partial\Omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary assumes only that S_R is a boundary component of the subdomain omega; it may be an interior interface of Omega. The cited Friedrichs theorem requires S_R to lie in the boundary of Omega itself, yet the proof applies its constant C_F to obtain an L^2(Omega) estimate. Thus the dependency is used outside its hypotheses.

failure_location.quote:

some }\omega\subset\Omega\text{ such that }S_{R}\text{ is a relatively closed
subset of }\partial\omega,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that S_R is relatively closed in the boundary of Omega, or prove a generalized Friedrichs estimate for an internal spherical interface with the same global L^2(Omega) conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: Both the L^2 estimate and the ensuing wavenumber-indexed trace estimate are unsupported for the corollary's stated geometry.
issues.title: The trace corollary applies the Friedrichs theorem without its boundary hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding the missing boundary hypothesis is a limited but substantive restriction of the stated geometric scope; preserving the current scope requires a new contained lemma.
